newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Rugby Union-Whelan says no need for panic.
newsitem.headline: Rugby Union-Whelan says no need for panic.

text.p: Ireland manager Pat Whelan said on Wednesday there was no need for panic after his side had been beaten 40-25 by Western Samoa in a one-off international at Lansdowne Road.

"There is no need to panic. If you look at the territorial situation, we actually had 70 percent of the territory. What we didn't do is convert that in to points and in addition to that we missed a lot of first time tackles," Whelan said.
"Once that happens against an international team like the Samoans you are in serious trouble," he added.
Western Samoa ran in five tries to Ireland's one and were never really troubled on their way to a deserved triumph.
Ireland will now have to re-group and prepare for the visit of Australia to Lansdowne Road on November 23.
"There is no doubt about it, we will improve. We've been down before but Irish teams are resilient and we will be back," Whelan said. -- Damien Lynch, Dublin Newsroom +353 1 6603377
